---
title: Use your own models
description: Use models from OpenRouter, Ollama, your own Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI or Google API key, or any OpenAI-compatible server in chat, the Advisor and Help, with or without GitHub Copilot.
---

Fabricator's model pickers can offer models from other providers, next to the models in your
GitHub Copilot plan, or instead of them:

| Provider | Models | Billed to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic** | Claude models | Your Anthropic account |
| **OpenAI** | GPT models | Your OpenAI account |
| **xAI** | Grok models | Your xAI account |
| **Google** | Gemini and Gemma models | The Google Cloud project your key belongs to |
| **OpenRouter** | Models from many makers on one key | Your OpenRouter account |
| **Ollama** | Open models that run on this computer | Nobody: they run on your own hardware |
| **OpenAI-compatible server** | Models from LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM or another server with an OpenAI-compatible API | Whoever runs the server |

Fabricator runs the conversation on your computer either way: it reads and edits your project
the same way, and it calls the provider whenever you choose one of its models. You don't need
to be signed in to GitHub Copilot to use them. See
[Use Fabricator without GitHub Copilot](#use-fabricator-without-github-copilot).

## Open Model providers

Your models are set up in **Model providers**, in **Accounts**. To open it, do one of these:

- In a model picker, select **Manage model providers…** at the bottom, or **Add your own
  models…** in its list of models.
- In **Settings**, select **Manage model providers**.
- On the setup screen, under **Connect GitHub Copilot**, select **Use your own models
  instead**.

## Add an API key

For Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Google and OpenRouter:

1. In **Model providers**, find the provider and select **Add key**.
2. Paste your key into the box. To create one, select **Get a key**, which opens the
   provider's key page in your browser.
3. Select **Save key**.

Fabricator checks the key with the provider before it keeps it. If the provider turns it
down, you see a message such as "OpenAI didn't accept this key. Check that you copied all of
it." and nothing is saved.

![Model providers in Accounts: an Anthropic key saved, with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 turned on for the model pickers, and an OpenAI key being added](/screenshots/model-providers.webp)

When the key works, the card shows **API key** and where it's kept, such as "Saved in
Windows Credential Manager". On macOS, keys are kept in your Keychain.

OpenRouter offers hundreds of models from many makers on one key, so Fabricator lists only
the ones that can call tools, which its agent needs. Type in the box above the list to find a
model.

## Connect Ollama

[Ollama](https://ollama.com) runs open models on your own computer, so there's no key and
nothing to pay per use.

1. Install Ollama, and pull a model that can call tools, such as `gpt-oss:20b` or `qwen3`:

   ```bash
   ollama pull gpt-oss:20b
   ```

2. In Ollama's settings, set **Context length** to 64k or more. Fabricator's agent sends long
   instructions and parts of your app with every request, and Ollama gives models a short
   context unless you change it. Fabricator checks the context length with each request, and
   stops with a message when it's too short.
3. In **Model providers**, under **Ollama**, select **Connect**.
4. Check **Ollama address**. On this computer, it's `http://localhost:11434`. To use Ollama on
   another computer, enter that computer's address.
5. Select **Connect**.

Fabricator lists the models you pulled that can call tools, and turns on the three you pulled
last. If Ollama isn't running, you see "Ollama isn't answering at http://localhost:11434. Start
Ollama, then try again." If none of your models can call tools, pull one that can, then select
**Check again**.

> [!TIP]
> Local models are slower than cloud models, and smaller ones can struggle with large changes.
> Pick the biggest model your computer runs well, and keep requests focused.

## Connect an OpenAI-compatible server

Any server with an OpenAI-compatible API works, such as LM Studio, vLLM or a LiteLLM proxy.

1. Start the server, and load a model that can call tools.
2. In **Model providers**, under **OpenAI-compatible server**, select **Connect**.
3. In **OpenAI-compatible server address**, enter the address of its API, such as
   `http://localhost:1234/v1` for LM Studio. If you leave out `/v1`, Fabricator tries it too.
4. If the server needs a key, enter it in **API key (optional)**.
5. Select **Connect**.

Fabricator lists every model the server offers. It assumes a 128k-token context window unless
the server reports one.

## Choose which models the pickers show

Under **In the model pickers**, each card lists the models the provider offers, with each
model's context window, and `images` when it can read images. The models marked
**Recommended** are turned on when you add a key or connect a server. A model marked
**Retiring** is one the provider is phasing out.

- Turn a model on or off with its checkbox. The pickers update right away.
- Select **Show all** to see every model the provider offers. In a long list, type in the box
  above it to find a model.
- Select **Check again** to check the provider again and update its list of models.

## Pick one of your models

1. In the chat composer, open the model pill.
2. Select **Model**, or, while **Auto** is on, the row that says how many models you can choose
   from, such as **Choose from 32 models**. Choosing a model turns Auto off.
3. Choose a model under **Your models**. The provider's name is next to each one, or **Your
   server** for one on an OpenAI-compatible server.

![The model picker with Auto off, the model list open, Copilot's models with their makers' logos, and the models on the user's own Anthropic and OpenAI keys under Your models](/screenshots/model-picker.webp)

The pill shows a key next to a model that runs on your own API key, and a server next to one
that runs on Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server. To change your models, select **Manage
model providers…** at the bottom of the picker.

The same picker is in the **Advisor** bar. See
[Choose a model and reasoning effort](/docs/build/chat#choose-a-model-and-reasoning-effort).

You can switch models at any time, also in the middle of a conversation. The next message
uses the model you chose.

## Use Fabricator without GitHub Copilot

You don't need GitHub Copilot when you have a model of your own. On the setup screen, under
**Connect GitHub Copilot**, select **Use your own models instead**, set up a provider, then
select **Done**. The step then says **Using your own models**, and you can enter Fabricator.

While you're not signed in to GitHub Copilot:

- The model pickers offer only your own models, and there's no **Auto**. The picker says
  "You're not signed in to GitHub Copilot, so chats run on your own models."
- A chat set to **Auto**, to one of Copilot's models, or to one of your models that you've
  since removed or turned off runs on your default model instead: the model your
  [chat defaults](/docs/reference/settings) use when it's one of your own, else the first of
  your models in the picker. The model pill shows which one.
- The Advisor, Help and the other features that use a model run on your own models too.

To use Copilot's models again, sign in to GitHub Copilot in **Accounts**.

## Models that can't read images

Some models can't read images. While one of them is selected, **Image** in the composer's
**+** menu says that the model can't read images. If you already attached images, Fabricator
holds the message until you remove them or choose a model that can read images.

## Replace or remove a key or server

- To use a different key, select **Replace**, paste the new key, and select **Replace key**.
  Fabricator keeps the old key if the provider doesn't accept the new one.
- To change a server's address, select **Change**, enter the new address, and select
  **Connect**. For an OpenAI-compatible server, enter its key again if it needs one.
- To remove a key or a server, select **Remove**, then select **Remove** again to confirm. Its
  models leave the pickers. A chat or the Advisor set to one of them asks you to choose
  another model, or, while you're not signed in to GitHub Copilot, runs on your default model.

## Plans and limits

A cloud provider bills your account for what its models use, and its plan sets your limits.
Fabricator's requests are large: each one carries Fabricator's instructions, tools and parts
of your app. To see how many tokens a chat has used on your models, see
[See what a chat has used](/docs/build/chat#see-what-a-chat-has-used).

- Some plans cap the tokens a key can use a minute, so a smaller plan may turn these
  requests down. If that happens, Fabricator says, for example, "This request is bigger than
  your OpenAI plan allows per minute." Upgrade your plan with the provider, or choose
  another model.
- Google's free tier allows only a few requests a minute and a day. If Fabricator says
  "Google is limiting how often your key can be used", wait and try again, or turn on
  billing for your key's Google Cloud project.
- Ollama and other servers you run have no bill, but they're limited by your hardware. Keep
  Ollama's context length at 64k or more. With less, Fabricator stops a turn on an Ollama
  model and says so.

For other errors from a provider, see
[A model on your own API key shows an error](/docs/troubleshooting/chat#a-model-on-your-own-api-key-shows-an-error).

## Your keys and privacy

- Fabricator keeps your keys in Windows Credential Manager, or in your Keychain on macOS.
  They never go into Fabricator's settings, logs or diagnostics, and Fabricator never shows
  a saved key. It keeps the address of a server you connect in its settings.
- When you use one of your models, Fabricator on your computer sends your request and the
  project context it needs straight to the provider, under the provider's terms for your
  account. With Ollama on your computer, nothing leaves it.
- Requests to OpenAI, xAI, Google, OpenRouter, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers pass
  through a relay on your computer that adapts them to what each API accepts: for example, it
  leaves out a reasoning effort a model doesn't take. With each request to Ollama, it also asks
  Ollama what context length the model runs with. Nothing leaves your computer through it
  except the request to that provider. While Fabricator runs, the relay keeps the signatures
  Gemini adds to its tool calls in memory, to send them back with the conversation.

See [Privacy](/docs/reference/privacy#your-own-models).
